I will plant winter wheat and summer maize on the same land. In my place in Quzhou County, this is the steadiest way for me to farm through the year. I know this rotation well, the buyers are easy to find, and the work schedule fits my labor and experience. I do not want to take big risks on crops with harder management or unstable prices. Wheat gives me a safe main crop, and maize follows right after harvest, so the land does not sit idle.

I will keep the plan simple and practical. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, stronger disease resistance, and better yield. I will not overuse fertilizer because that wastes money and can push weak growth or lodging. I will put most attention on base fertilizer, the key watering times, and a few timely pesticide sprays only when needed. For wheat, I will prepare the field well and manage water carefully in spring. For maize, I will sow quickly after wheat harvest, keep moisture in the soil, and focus on seedling protection, weed control, and grain filling. This is the plan I would trust for a steady year.
